words.meaning: The bearing of fruit or the process of making productive or fruitful, combining the ideas of harvest and joy in natural abundance.
words.sentence1: The orchard is in a state of abundant fructification this season, bringing great joy to the farmers. (The orchard is in a state of abundant fructification this season, bringing great joy to the farmers.)
words.sentence2: Their hard work finally led to the fructification of their long-term project. (Their hard work finally led to the fructification of their long-term project.)

words.meaning: A state of intense joy, rejoicing, or celebration, often associated with a festive gathering or harvest feast.
words.sentence1: El pueblo celebró con gran jubileo la llegada de la cosecha. (The town celebrated the arrival of the harvest with great jubilee.)
words.sentence2: Había un ambiente de jubileo en las calles durante las festividades. (There was an atmosphere of jubilee in the streets during the festivities.)

words.meaning: A state of being intoxicated with joy, excitement, or the rich abundance of nature.
words.sentence1: L'enivrement des sens était total au milieu des vignes mûres. (The intoxication of the senses was complete in the middle of the ripe vineyards.)
words.sentence2: Il ressentait un profond enivrement en regardant le fruit de son travail. (He felt a deep intoxication when looking at the fruit of his labor.)

words.meaning: The specific joy, gladness, or delight felt during and because of the harvest.
words.sentence1: Die Erntefreude war den Bauern ins Gesicht geschrieben, als sie die Körner einbrachten. (The joy of harvest was written on the farmers' faces as they brought in the grains.)
words.sentence2: Ein Gefühl von Erntefreude erfüllte das ganze Dorf nach der erfolgreichen Arbeit. (A feeling of harvest joy filled the entire village after the successful work.)

words.meaning: A bountiful harvest or rich crop, embodying the joy of agricultural abundance.
words.sentence1: Kotoshi wa kessaku de, machi juu ga houjyou no yorokobi ni tsutsumareta. (This year was a masterpiece, and the whole town was wrapped in the joy of a bountiful harvest.)
words.sentence2: Nouka wa houjyou o kansha shite matsuri o okonatta. (The farmers held a festival in gratitude for the bountiful harvest.)

words.meaning: Exultation, a lively and triumphant joy, fitting for a successful gathering of crops.
words.sentence1: Ci fu grande esultanza tra i contadini quando raccolsero l'ultimo cesto. (There was great exultation among the farmers when they gathered the last basket.)
words.sentence2: L'esultanza per la buona annata si diffuse in tutta la valle. (The exultation for the good year spread throughout the valley.)

words.meaning: An atmosphere of joy, festivity, and gladness often associated with celebrations and successful harvest seasons.
words.sentence1: Cūnzi lǐ dōu chōngmǎn zhe nóngdù de xǐqì, yīnwèi shōucéng hǎo. (The whole village is filled with a strong atmosphere of joy because the harvest is good.)
words.sentence2: Zhè zhǒng xǐqì ràng měi gè rén dōu gǎndào hěn wēnnuǎn. (This kind of festivity and joy makes everyone feel very warm.)

words.meaning: The fortunate harvest or the blessing of gathered crops bringing prosperity and gladness.
words.sentence1: Deulpanui bokchae-reul bomyeo ma-eumi deundeunhaejyeotda. (Seeing the blessed harvest of the fields made my heart feel secure and joyful.)
words.sentence2: Olhaeui bokchae-neun uri gajogege keun gippeum-eul ju-eotda. (This year's abundant harvest gave our family great joy.)

words.meaning: Sacred, blessed, or auspicious, often describing the fruitful rewards and joyful bounty bestowed by nature.
words.sentence1: Pka phkar del ban douh jeung neng pteal saksit chol del ban chomneanh. (The flowers that grew in the sacred soil brought forth a victorious and joyful harvest.)
words.sentence2: Preah thngai nou pteal saksit nih ban trov kar chorng. (The sun upon this blessed land has brought about a joyful reaping.)

words.meaning: Fertility or fruitfulness, representing the productive earth that yields a joyful harvest.
words.sentence1: Die vrugbaarheid van die grond het vanjaar 'n wonderlike oes opgelewer. (The fertility of the soil yielded a wonderful harvest this year.)
words.sentence2: Ons is dankbaar vir die vrugbaarheid en die vreugde wat dit bring. (We are grateful for the fertility and the joy that it brings.)
